problem_text:
A logistics manager must allocate a fleet of cargo drones to transport a selection of specialized equipment modules to a remote research station. The goal is to maximize the total utility score of the delivered modules, while adhering to the drones' collective maximum lift capacity.

The available equipment modules are:
* Module A: mass 39kg, utility 179 credits
* Module B: mass 18kg, utility 49 credits
* Module C: mass 30kg, utility 91 credits
* Module D: mass 7kg, utility 272 credits
* Module E: mass 17kg, utility 296 credits
* Module F: mass 46kg, utility 217 credits
* Module G: mass 39kg, utility 239 credits
* Module H: mass 27kg, utility 91 credits
* Module I: mass 39kg, utility 224 credits
* Module J: mass 50kg, utility 74 credits
* Module K: mass 44kg, utility 67 credits
* Module L: mass 38kg, utility 67 credits
* Module M: mass 12kg, utility 256 credits
* Module N: mass 19kg, utility 61 credits
* Module O: mass 44kg, utility 227 credits
* Module P: mass 17kg, utility 151 credits
* Module Q: mass 8kg, utility 192 credits

A critical compatibility requirement dictates that exactly one of Module A and Module B must be included in the shipment.

Furthermore, if Module C is selected, it necessitates a dedicated support apparatus that reduces the effective available lift capacity by 10 kg.
The entire drone fleet can sustain a maximum lift mass of 345 kg. The manager must determine the optimal set of modules to dispatch.
